report.summary: Cleared the project's only remaining compile warnings (three partially initialised timer configs in app_mqtt) and left the emulated Wi-Fi driver crash alone — four identical crashes after three product-side attempts made further radio churn unjustified. Builds at 2.94 MB, 20 % free.
decisions: The reported failure is the fourth byte-identical crash (same unmapped PC, same cycle count) inside the emulated Wi-Fi driver's probe-request path, after three different product-side sequencing changes and with no product frame on the path. Both the functional report and the review now conclude the same thing, so I did not change the radio again — that would be churn, not a fix. It stays a documented hardware question.

I fixed the one thing in this round that is genuinely the product's: the three partially designated esp_timer_create_args_t initialisers in app_mqtt were the only project-code warnings in the build (nine of them), which makes a future real one invisible. Zero-init then assign.

Left the two owner-level deviations alone again: adding a whole-number 21 phrase changes what the device listens for, and restoring SET+MODE changes how it wipes itself — both are the spec's behaviour, not mine to redefine without a decision.
report.build: esp32s31 success — 0x2cd410 (2937872 B) in a 0x380000 partition, 20% free; the app_mqtt compile step now emits no warnings from product code; check_code clean

findingsAddressed.finding: info — nine -Wmissing-field-initializers warnings in app_mqtt (partially designated esp_timer_create_args_t)
findingsAddressed.fix: all three initialisers zero-initialised then assigned (net debounce, Wi-Fi retry, AP idle timer) — the build's project-code warning channel is clean again

findingsAddressed.finding: info — commissioned-reboot crash inside the Wi-Fi driver (4th identical round)
findingsAddressed.fix: unchanged by design: evidence is conclusive that it is the emulated driver's scan path, not product logic; carried as a hardware question with the exact fault signature

findingsAddressed.finding: info — standing deviations (single-button factory reset, no 'set the office to 21' phrase)
findingsAddressed.fix: unchanged pending the owner's decision; both flagged in the previous rounds and again here

openQuestions: The commissioned-reboot behaviour on real silicon is the one open stability question; if it reproduces there, the lever is the Wi-Fi driver's scan/init configuration rather than app_mqtt's sequencing.
The voice vocabulary gap and the factory-reset gesture need a decision from the owner before I change behaviour the spec describes.
